learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the principles and key aspects of fluid mechanics for rigorous application in engineering.
Be able to apply knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve thermofluidodynamic problems from first principles.
Be able to choose, simplify, and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in thermofluidodynamic systems.
Have an understanding of different approximation methods in fluid mechanics and the ability to use them in solving engineering problems.
Learn to locate and appropriately use specialized scientific and technical bibliography in fundamental and applied fluid mechanics.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve fluid engineering problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in fluid engineering and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
An adequate knowledge of their engineering branch that includes some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Summary of conservation equations in integral and differential form. Initial and boundary conditions.
Unidirectional steady and unsteady motion. Quasi-steady limit.
Lubrication theory. Motion in slender channels and thin layers dominated by viscous forces. The wedge effect. Reynolds equation. Applications.
High Reynolds number flow. Ideal internal and external flow. Compressible flow.
Boundary layer theory. Separation. Integral methods.
assessment_rules: The final exam accounts for 60% of the grade, and continuous assessment for 40%. Continuous assessment is based on submission exercises (40%), in-class exercises (40%), and practical reports (20%). It is possible to pass the subject without taking the final exam. For students who fail continuous assessment, the ordinary exam counts for 60%, with the remaining 40% from continuous assessment. For the extraordinary exam, the grade can be 100% from the extraordinary exam, or 60% from the extraordinary exam plus 40% from continuous assessment, choosing the most favorable option for the student.
